# JusPrin's translations JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for (`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new entry in every `.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's `AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: ` where the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder. The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like `<0>…` for elements inside a `Trans`, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). ## Marking text Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items, tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly as it was. Leave these in English, unmarked: - **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown. - Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes, test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code. - Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`, `report_error`): they are read by developers. - Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names. ### In the pages ```tsx import { t, plural } from '@lingui/core/macro'; import { Trans } from '@lingui/react/macro';

Takes effect when {app} restarts. Your project is saved first.

const label = plural(count, { one: '# printer', other: '# printers' }); const title = t({ message: 'Back', context: 'navigation' }); // a word with several meanings const hint = t({ message: 'Fit', comment: 'Verb: scale the model to the plate' }); // a note for translators ``` - One message per sentence. Never build a sentence from translated pieces, and never splice a translated word into another sentence: use a placeholder, or a `Trans` with the element inside it. - A count needs `plural` / `Plural`, not "printer(s)". - Put only plain variables in placeholders (`{name}`, not `{a.b.c}`): the translator sees the variable's name. Pull an expression into a well-named local first. - The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no provider (see `i18n.tsx`). - Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps working. ### In the native code - `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for JSON sent to a page. - Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs before the language is loaded. Mark such a table with `L("…")` and call `_L`/`_u8L` on the entry where it is shown. - Use `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)` rather than concatenation, and `_L_PLURAL` for counts; `// TRN` above a string tells the translator what it means. - Every file that marks text is extracted: `update_catalogs.py` reads every `.cpp` and `.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` except `Testing/`. Do not add JusPrin files to `localization/i18n/list.txt`. # Translation rules The rules a translation must follow, condensed from the wiki's [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md), the [glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) and the localization section of `AGENTS.md`. `po_tool.py apply` rejects the mechanical violations it can detect; everything else is on the translator. ## Mechanical: enforced by `apply` A rejected entry is not written. Fix it and apply again. - **Placeholders stay exactly as written:** `%s`, `%d`, `%.1f`, `%1$d`, `%1%`, `%%`. Never `%1 %`, never `%` for `%%`. Plain printf placeholders keep their order; only positional ones (`%1$s`, `%1%`) may move, and one the msgid repeats may appear just once. A broken placeholder crashes the app. - **Line breaks:** the same number of `\n`, with the same leading and trailing ones. Don't add breaks to fit text, least of all in parameter names. - **Leading and trailing spaces** are kept. A leading space usually means the string is appended to another. - **HTML tags** are kept, and the text between them is translated: `Click here to install it.` - **`℃`** (U+2103) stays one character, written exactly as in the source: `%d℃`, never `°C`, `° C` or `%d ℃`. - **Tokens stay verbatim:** `{placeholders}`, `[macros]`, G-code commands (`M141`, `G28`). Setting keys in snake_case (`use_relative_e_distances`) are flagged as warnings, because a few snake_case msgids are really labels (`top_front`). Keep a key unless the string uses it as a display name. - **Plural entries** need every form from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (`nplurals`: 1 for ja/ko/zh/th/vi, 3 for ru/cs/pl/lt, 4 for uk). Each form is really inflected for its quantity. Repeating one sentence is a bug in Slavic and Baltic languages, but correct in Turkish and Hungarian. ## A person's translation: patch it, don't rewrite it A translator's wording is kept unless it is wrong. Machine output never replaces it wholesale. - **A reworded string:** `pending` lists earlier translations of similar English under `similar`, and marks a person's work with `"human": true`. When the English barely changed, start from that translation and change only what the English change requires: a renamed term, an added clause, a period. Keep the translator's wording, word order, terms and line structure. If they already wrote what the new English says, the translation does not change at all. - **A fix in a person's translation:** for a check error (a line break, a space, placeholder order, a missing clause), change only what the error needs. Keep the rest of their words, even where they differ from the glossary or from how you would phrase it. Report such glossary differences instead. - **Rewrite only what is plainly wrong:** another string's text, a cut-off sentence, a mistranslation. Say why with `"rewrite": ""` in the item; the reason becomes the review note. - `apply` enforces this. It rejects text that strays further from a person's translation than the English change explains (below 85% alike for a fix, or clearly less alike than the English for a reworded string), unless the item carries `rewrite`. - Apply a fix that keeps the person's words with `--human`, so the entry stays theirs. Text you wrote gets the default `# AI Translated`. ## Mechanical: not detectable, still required - Edit only `msgstr`. Never change `msgid`, `msgctxt`, the header or another entry's text. - **Ending punctuation follows the source:** no added period, and no dropped one. `apply` warns. - Units follow the SI convention of the language: `s`, not `sec`. A parameter description holds no unit, because the field shows it. - **A button or short label holds one translation:** no alternatives in parentheses. They widen the control. - Don't use `fuzzy` for uncertainty. Fuzzy entries are hidden, and users then see English. ## Context: know what the string is before choosing its words English reuses one word for different things, and a string seen alone often reads several ways. Settle what each entry is before translating it. `pending` gives every entry the context the source holds: `refs` (where it is used), `code` (the lines around the use, for short strings and placeholder strings) and `nearby` (the translated short strings used next to it). `lookup --code` shows the same for existing entries. The catalogs themselves carry no source references. - **What kind of text it is,** from `code`: a button or menu item is a command, a field label or column header names a value, a checkbox states something that is on or off, and a tooltip, status line, error or dialog title each have their own register. Keep a label as short as a label. - **What it belongs to.** A setting's strings sit together in `PrintConfig.cpp`: `this->add("", …)`, then `label`, `category`, `tooltip`, `sidetext`. The tooltip describes that option, and quotes the label exactly as `nearby` shows it translated. The items of one menu, choice or toolbar (`enum_labels`, `Append`, an array of names) are a set: give them one grammatical form, and words that tell them apart. - **`msgctxt` separates homonyms.** `Back` in *Camera View* is the rear view, and `Back` in *Navigation* is the go-back button. Translate each context on its own. - **Overloaded English: translate the meaning.** - *Flow ratio* is a multiplier, *Flow Rate* is throughput, and *Flow Dynamics* is pressure compensation. These are three different terms. - *Extruder* can mean the toolhead, the feeder motor ("High extruder current on filament swap") or the nozzle ("all extruders must have the same diameter"). - *Home* is the homing move ("Please home all axes"), the home page, or the Home key (*Keyboard Shortcut*), which takes the name printed on that language's keyboards. *Fill* is infill, gap fill, or the paint tools' bucket and smart fill. *Normal* is the ordinary kind ("Normal support", "Normal printing") or the surface normal ("Normal X", "Smooth normals"). *Model* is the 3D model, or the printer model in "Model:". *Process* is the process preset, or an operation under way ("the slicing process"). - The glossary's rows record the senses that recur (`Plate` versus `Bed / Build plate`, `Feature (print)` versus `Feature (Design)`); the code tells which one a string means. - **Check the meaning in the code** when the English leaves it open: read the call site, and further in the file when `code` is not enough. - See what each placeholder is filled with. A fallback string substituted into a sentence must fit the slot it fills. - Settle the semantics the English blurs: a ratio or a difference, which way a rotation turns, which control a hint names. - **A msgid used in several places** (`left` is a view name and a hotend; `Sphere` is a primitive and a paint brush) needs a wording that fits every use. When none can, report the missing `msgctxt` as a source problem. - **When the context still leaves two readings,** take the likelier one and add a review note naming the other. ## Choosing the words - **The glossary is binding.** Use the language's rendering for every glossary term the `pending` output lists, inflected as the sentence needs. - **Rows that share a base term are different senses:** `Seam` (the print seam) versus `Seam (UV)` (the unwrap cut), and `Instance` versus `Instance (application)`. Pick by the description. - **A qualified row may be a false match.** `Feature (Design)` does not apply to "features of the app". - **A cell marked ⚠ (or holding two renderings) is unsettled.** Use the form the catalog already uses for that sense (`lookup`), and flag the entry for review. - **Kept in English:** brand and product names (OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, Orca Cloud, AMS, Micro-Lidar), acronyms (FDM, LAN, HTTPS), file formats, material codes (PLA, PETG-CF), G-code, macros and variables stay as written. In "Adaptive Pressure Advance", only "Pressure Advance" stays English. See the glossary page's *Kept in English* table. - **Language specifics** on the glossary page (`po_tool.py glossary --lang L` prints them) override general habits for that language. - **The catalog's existing words come next.** A tooltip or message that names a setting, a button or a menu item quotes that control's translation exactly, so the text matches what the user sees. `nearby` shows the controls next to the string; `lookup` finds the rest. For a recurring term the glossary lacks, `lookup` the English and `lookup --msgstr` the rendering you intend, and use the one the catalog already settled on in that sense. Reuse obsolete (`#~`) entries as a translation memory. - **No settled term: look outside the catalog, in this order.** 1. **Other slicers' shipped catalogs** for the same language: [BambuStudio](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio) `bbl/i18n//BambuStudio_.po` and [PrusaSlicer](https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer) `resources/localization//PrusaSlicer_.po` (a local clone, if there is one). Orca shares much of its UI with both, so their translators have often rendered the same string already. Their choice is evidence, not a rule: the glossary and Orca's own catalog win. 2. **The 3D-printing community in that language:** manuals, wikis and forums of printer vendors (Bambu Lab, Prusa, Creality, Snapmaker) and their users. Take the term printers actually use, a loanword where they use the loanword. 3. **Neighbouring fields,** when printing has no term of its own: CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion, Onshape, AutoCAD), CNC/CAM and machining, then engineering and mathematics. General UI vocabulary (*Settings*, *Preferences*, *Undo*, *Browse*, *Quit*, *Copy*, *Paste*) follows the operating systems' own translations, which users already know. 4. **English,** when nothing is established: brand names, acronyms, file formats, G-code tokens, variables, and Orca-specific feature names with no equivalent. Translate paired terms as a pair, so they read as the two sides of one choice (direct drive and Bowden, inner and outer wall). Name the sources a term came from in the report. - **Each field keeps its own vocabulary.** 3D-view and CAD strings follow CAD software and drafting standards: the standard view names, *isometric*, *orbit*, *pan* and *zoom*, *cut plane* versus *section plane*, the primitive names. The camera of the 3D view (the viewpoint) and the printer's camera (the device) are different things and take different words wherever the language has two. - **A regional variant is its own language.** Never derive one from the other character by character or word by word: zh_TW and zh_CN differ in vocabulary, not only in script. Start from the variant's own glossary column and catalog. A converter (OpenCC `s2twp` for zh_CN → zh_TW) gives a draft at most; review every entry it produced. - **Boilerplate stays uniform.** `Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?` and `If expressed as a %, it will be computed over …` each get one template in the language, even where the English varies. ## Style - **Localize, don't translate word-for-word.** Translate what the string means where it appears (see *Context*), not each English word. - **Write native UI text.** The result should read as if the app had been written in that language. - Restructure the sentence instead of following English word order. - Break up long noun chains. - Drop passive and filler constructions the language doesn't use in UI text. - Don't calque English idioms or compounds where the language has its own expression. - Don't carry English Title Case over: capitalize as the language does (sentence case in most, German nouns as German writes them). - Use the language's own punctuation. Don't carry English marks over, such as ` — ` or straight quotes where the language has its own. ASCII quotes around a literal value the user types or the app matches stay as written. - **Follow the catalog's conventions,** which a new entry must match: - formal or informal address; - full-width or half-width punctuation; - spacing between scripts (CJK next to Latin letters or digits); - the separator sibling labels use before their value; - the verb form of buttons and menu commands (infinitive, imperative or noun); - the form of a confirmation question. - **Simplify developer phrasing** when the meaning survives. *"This option determines whether OrcaSlicer should apply the retract reduction on infill"* reads better as *"Disable retractions while printing infill."* Introduce nuances in following sentences, not in one packed clause. - **Don't expand.** A machine translation adds no facts the English doesn't state. Expanding descriptions is for human translators, who can confirm the extra content. - **Write for both audiences:** professionals and people with a printer at home. Keep the established terminology, used as plainly as the string allows. - **Read the batch back without the English** before applying it, as a user of the app would see it. Rewrite whatever reads like a translation, is ambiguous on its own, or uses a word differently from the strings around it. ## When to add a review note Add `"review": ""` to an item when the translation is probable but unconfirmed. It becomes `# Needs human review: …`, and the entry still ships. Typical reasons: - The English stays ambiguous even with its code: "Tile" as a verb or a noun. - A short label's role shows only in the running app, not in its code. - Two established terms compete, or the glossary cell is unsettled. - The string's grammar depends on a value substituted at runtime: `%zu %s` counts with no plural entry. Say exactly what to look at and where: *"Row name in the Design tab tool-offer menu; check it reads right for the whole row."* ## Problems that belong in the source, not the translation Report these; don't work around them in a catalog. - **The English is wrong.** Never "fix" it in the translation only. - **A hint names a control that doesn't exist,** or a user-visible literal isn't wrapped in `_L`. - **One msgid needs two translations.** The source needs `_L_CONTEXT` / `_u8L_CONTEXT` (a code change). - **A literal `%` in a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format`** fails `msgfmt`. The fix is a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source, not `%%` in the translation. src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/: JusPrin.pot ca.po cs.po de.po es.po eu.po fr.po hu.po it.po ja.po ko.po lt.po nl.po pl.po pt_BR.po ru.po sv.po th.po tr.po uk.po vi.po zh_CN.po zh_TW.po src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/: ca.po cs.po de.po en.po es.po eu.po fr.po hu.po it.po ja.po ko.po lt.po nl.po pl.po pt_BR.po ru.po sv.po th.po tr.po uk.po vi.po zh_CN.po zh_TW.po 1790 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/ca.po 3847 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/ca.po 5637 total M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/de.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/es.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/fr.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/it.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/ja.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/ko.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/pl.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/pt_BR.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/ru.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/zh_CN.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/native/zh_TW.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/de.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/es.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/fr.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/it.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/ko.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/ru.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/zh_CN.po M src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/pages/zh_TW.po

256 ca-glossary.tsv
﻿English	Description	ca
Infill	Material printed inside the walls to give the part its strength.	Farciment
Sparse infill	The low-density infill of the part interior, whose density and pattern are configurable.	Farciment poc dens
Pattern	The line layout used to fill a region — applies to surfaces (top and bottom), to fills such as sparse or internal solid infill, and to ironing.	Patró
Rectilinear	Pattern of parallel straight lines — the default fill for most solid regions and supports. Shares its root with the Aligned Rectilinear, Rectilinear grid and Rectilinear Interlaced variants; keep all four consistent.	Rectilini
Concentric	Pattern of nested loops that follow the region outline. One of the center-based patterns, together with Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords and Octagram Spiral.	Concèntric
Aligned Rectilinear	Rectilinear variant whose lines keep the same angle on every layer instead of alternating. Keep the Rectilinear root recognizable across the whole family.	Alineat Rectilini
Rectilinear grid	Support base pattern of crossed rectilinear lines forming a grid. Distinct from Rectilinear Interlaced — the two are separate dropdown options and must not share a translation.	Quadrícula rectilínia
Rectilinear Interlaced	Support interface pattern whose rectilinear lines alternate direction between layers. Distinct from Rectilinear grid — the two must not share a translation.	Entrellaçat Rectilini
Monotonic	Fill ordering that lays every line down in one consistent direction for a uniform surface finish. The mathematical sense, not the everyday "monotonous".	Monotònic
Monotonic line	Monotonic variant that keeps each line continuous. Keep the same root as Monotonic.	Línia monotònica
Zig Zag	Infill pattern of connected back-and-forth lines. Distinct from the Snake print order, which also walks a serpentine path.	Zig Zag
Cross Zag	Zig Zag variant that rotates the pattern between layers. Keep the Zag family recognizable together.	Cross Zag
Locked Zag	Zig Zag variant whose layers interlock for added strength. Keep the Zag family recognizable together.	Locked Zag
Grid	Infill and support interface pattern of two crossing sets of lines. The pattern name — not the build plate or preview grid.	Graella
Triangles	Infill pattern of three crossing sets of lines forming triangles.	Triangles
Tri-hexagon	Infill pattern combining triangles and hexagons.	Tri-hexàgon
Cubic	Infill pattern of stacked cubes standing on a corner. Root of the Adaptive Cubic, Quarter Cubic and Support Cubic variants.	Cúbic
Adaptive Cubic	Cubic variant that subdivides towards the part surface, denser near the shell than in the core. Keep the Cubic root.	Cúbic adaptatiu
Quarter Cubic	Cubic variant built from quarter-offset cells. Keep the Cubic root.	Quart cúbic
Support Cubic	Very sparse Cubic variant meant to hold up top surfaces rather than add strength. Keep the Cubic root.	Suport Cúbic
Lightning	Pattern that grows only branching supports under top surfaces and leaves the rest hollow. Used both as a sparse infill and as a support base pattern.	Llampec
Honeycomb	Infill pattern of hexagonal cells. Root of the 3D Honeycomb and Lateral Honeycomb variants.	Panal d'abella
3D Honeycomb	Honeycomb variant whose cell walls shift with height. Keep the Honeycomb root.	Panal d'abella 3D
Lateral Honeycomb	Honeycomb variant oriented sideways for lateral strength. Keep the Honeycomb root.	Panal d'abella lateral
Lateral Lattice	Infill pattern of sideways-oriented lattice cells.	Gelosia 2D
Cross Hatch	Infill pattern whose layers cross at alternating angles.	Quadrícula
TPMS-D	Infill based on the Schwarz D (Diamond) triply periodic minimal surface. TPMS is an acronym and Schwarz a proper name; most catalogs keep the label verbatim.	TPMS-D
TPMS-FK	Infill based on the Fischer-Koch S triply periodic minimal surface. TPMS is an acronym and Fischer-Koch a proper name; most catalogs keep the label verbatim.	TPMS-FK
Gyroid	Infill pattern based on the gyroid minimal surface. Proper name of the surface.	Giroide
Hilbert Curve	Infill following the Hilbert space-filling curve. Named after the mathematician; keep the proper name.	Corba de Hilbert
Archimedean Chords	Center-based pattern following an Archimedean spiral. Named after Archimedes; keep the proper name.	Acords d'Arquimedes
Octagram Spiral	Center-based pattern that spirals outward as an eight-pointed star.	Octograma en Espiral
Spiral Inset	Center-based pattern whose nested loops are joined into one continuous inward spiral. Shares its shape with Concentric; keep the two distinct.	Espiral interior
Hollow	Support base pattern meaning no base pattern at all — the support interior is left empty. The Default for Tree supports.	Buit
Outer wall	The outermost perimeter loop of each layer — the surface the user sees.	Perímetre exterior
Inner wall	The perimeter loops printed behind the outer wall.	Perímetre interior
Wall loops	The number of perimeter loops (walls) printed around each layer.	Bucles de perímetre
Shell	The solid outer skin of the part — its walls plus the top and bottom layers.	Carcassa
Top	The upward-facing side of the print — its surfaces, shells and layers (Top surface, Top shell layers). Not the camera “Top view”, and not the text-alignment sense (msgctxt “Alignment”).	Superior
Bottom	The downward-facing side of the print, the one against the build plate — its surfaces, shells and layers (Bottom surface, Bottom shell layers). Not the camera “Bottom view”, and not the text-alignment sense (msgctxt “Alignment”).	Inferior
Fillet	A rounded transition between two edges or surfaces.	Arrodoniment
Chamfer	A flat, angled (beveled) transition between two edges or surfaces (contrast with a rounded Fillet).	Xamfrà
Brim	A flat band of extrusions around the first layer that improves bed adhesion.	Vora d'Adherència
Elephant foot	Bulging or flaring of the first layers, caused by the weight of the print pressing them out.	Peu d'elefant
Skirt	A loop printed around the object without touching it, to prime and stabilise the flow.	Faldilla
Draft shield	A tall wall printed around the model to shield it from drafts and keep chamber heat even.	Escut contra corrents d'aire
Raft	A printed platform under the object, used instead of printing on the bed directly.	Rai
Prime tower / Wipe tower	Tower printed beside the model to purge the nozzle after each filament change. Two English names for one object — see the note below.	Torre de Purga
Flush / Purge	Extruding filament to clear the previous material from the nozzle, e.g. at the prime tower on a filament change. Two English names for one action.	Purga
Interface layer	The prime tower layer where two materials meet and are purged into each other. Distinct from a support interface.	Capa d'interfície
PA Tower	Calibration model for tuning Pressure Advance.	Torre PA (Pressure Advance)
Ringing Tower	Calibration model that shows ringing/ghosting artifacts, used to tune input shaping.	Torre de Ringing
Fast Tower	Input-shaping calibration model printed at high speed and acceleration.	Torre ràpida
VFA	Vertical Fine Artifacts: faint repeating vertical wall marks, targeted by the VFA test. Acronym kept in English.	VFA
Artifacts	Unwanted visual defects on the printed surface.	Defectes
Bridge	An extrusion spanning a gap with no material beneath it.	Pont
Bridging	Printing a flat span across a gap between two supports, with no material beneath. See Bridge.	Ponts
Overhang	A downward-facing surface sloped beyond the angle the printer can print without support.	Voladís
Polyhole	A hole approximated as a many-sided polygon so it prints closer to round.	Poliforat
Ironing	A second, hot pass over top surfaces that smooths them.	Planxat
Seam	The visible start/end point of each perimeter loop on a layer.	Costura
Scarf joint	A seam split into a sloped, overlapping (scarfed) transition to hide it and add strength. The woodworking joint, not the clothing scarf.	Unió en bisell
Support	Printed structure that holds up overhangs and is removed after the print.	Suport
Tree supports	Organic, branch-shaped supports that touch the model at fewer points.	Suports d'arbre
Gap fill	Extra extrusions that fill thin spaces the walls are too wide to cover.	Farcir el buit
Fuzzy skin	Deliberately roughened outer surface, produced by jittering the wall path.	Pell difusa
Perlin	Fuzzy skin type: Proper name of the noise function. Smooth, natural-looking variations with coherent structure.	Perlin
Billow	Fuzzy skin type: Cloud-like noise pattern for fuzzy skin.	Billow
Ridged Multifractal	Fuzzy skin type: Noise pattern that produces sharp ridges.	Multifractal estriat
Voronoi	Fuzzy skin type: Cell-based noise pattern for fuzzy skin, named after the Voronoi diagram.	Voronoi
Ripple	Fuzzy skin type: Wave-like noise pattern for fuzzy skin.	Ripple
Nozzle	The replaceable tip the melt is pushed through; its bore sets the extrusion width.	Broquet
Hotend	The heated assembly — heat sink, heat break, heater block, heater cartridge, thermistor — that melts the filament and holds the nozzle. Not the nozzle alone, and not the extruder.	Hotend
Extruder	The motor and gears that push filament into the hotend; in multi-tool printers also a whole toolhead.	Extrusor
Extruder type	Whether the extruder is Direct Drive or Bowden.	Tipus d'extrusora
Direct Drive	Extruder mounted on the toolhead, directly above the hotend.	Direct Drive
Bowden	Extruder mounted on the frame, feeding filament through a PTFE tube to the hotend.	Bowden
Nozzle volume	The molten volume held inside the hotend, used to compute flushing on filament change.	Volum del broquet
Bed / Build plate	The heated print surface, i.e. the removable build plate, that the first layer sticks to. Two English names for one object.	Llit
Plate	One of the project's plates: each holds its own objects and is sliced and printed separately (Add plate, Slice plate, current plate). Where the language has a separate word, keep it apart from Bed / Build plate.	Placa
Build volume	The printable space of the printer — the build plate area times the maximum Z height.	Volum de construcció
Toolhead	The moving assembly that carries the hotend and nozzle (and on some printers the extruder).	Capçal
Chamber	The printer's enclosed build volume (the hardware enclosure itself, not its temperature setting).	Cambra
Part cooling fan	The fan that blows air onto freshly extruded plastic to solidify it.	Ventilador de refrigeració de peces
Exhaust fan	The fan that vents chamber air out of the enclosure.	Ventilador d'extracció
Cooling	Part-cooling settings that control fan behaviour during printing.	Refrigeració
Filament	The plastic feedstock on the spool.	Filament
Mixed filament	A filament slot made up of several physical filaments, printed as alternating sub-layers so their colors blend.	Filament mixt
Physical filament	A real filament loaded in the printer, as opposed to a mixed filament assembled from several of them.	Filament físic
Mixed filament gradient	Z-direction mode in which a mixed filament's sub-layer ratios shift gradually from one component to another as the print rises.	Degradat del filament mixt
Cool Plate	Bambu Lab low-temperature build plate, for PLA and PVA.	Base Freda
Engineering Plate	Bambu Lab high-temperature plate for engineering materials such as ABS, PC and PA.	Base d'Enginyeria
Textured PEI Plate	PEI-coated plate with a textured surface, leaving a matte finish on the bottom layer.	Base PEI amb Textura
Slice	Convert the model into layers and toolpaths — i.e. generate the G-code.	Laminar
Preset	A saved, selectable set of settings (print, filament or printer).	Perfil
Retraction	Pulling filament back to stop the nozzle oozing during travel moves.	Retracció
Unretract	Pushing filament forward again to resume extrusion after a retraction; the reverse of retraction.	Desretracció
Flow ratio	A multiplier on extrusion flow used to correct over- or under-extrusion.	Relació de flux
Flow Rate	The volume of material extruded per unit of time (mm³/s).	Cabal de flux
Flow Dynamics	Nozzle pressure-compensation calibration (the Pressure Advance factor). Keep it distinct from “Flow ratio” (an extrusion multiplier) and “Flow Rate” (volume per unit of time) — English often shortens all three to “flow”, but most languages need three different terms.	Dinàmiques de Flux
Volumetric Speed	Extrusion rate measured by volume rather than by distance (mm³/s).	Velocitat volumètrica
Ooze	Unwanted material seeping from the nozzle when it should not be extruding.	Prevenció de degoteig
Layer height	The thickness of a single printed layer.	Alçada de capa
Layer	One printed horizontal slice of the model.	Capa
Sublayer	One of the thin slices a layer is split into so the components of a mixed filament can be laid down in sequence.	Subcapa
Mixed color sublayer	The setting that splits layers containing mixed filaments into sub-layers to produce the color-blending effect.	Subcapa de color mixt
Line	A single extruded strand of material; also the wall/infill width-spacing unit.	Línia
Extrusion role	The function of an extrusion — outer wall, inner wall, infill, support, etc. — which sets its speed and parameters.	Rol d'extrusió
Contouring	Shaping a path or surface to follow the outline (contour) of the model.	Contornejat en Z
Jerk	The instantaneous speed change a machine allows at a corner; Marlin-style motion setting.	Jerk
Travel	A non-printing move between extrusions, with no material laid down.	Recorregut
Chamber temperature	The air temperature inside the printer's enclosure.	Temperatura de la cambra
Spiral vase	Mode that prints the object as one continuous single-wall spiral, with no layer seam.	Gerro en Espiral
Timelapse	Video assembled from one frame captured per layer.	Timelapse
Instance	An additional placement of one object on the plate, sharing that object’s geometry. Not Clone or Copy, which produce independent objects — “Fill bed with instances” and “Fill bed with copies” are different actions and must not share a translation. Not the running-application sense either — see Instance (application).	Instància
Instance (application)	A running copy of the application itself (“Allow only one OrcaSlicer instance”, “Failed to launch a new instance.”). A different sense from the object Instance on the plate — where a language uses the copy/duplicate word for the object sense, this one needs its own term.	Instància
Clone	Duplicating an object into independent objects, each with its own geometry, counted in “Number of copies”. Distinct from Instance, which only adds another placement of the same object.	Clonar
Mirror	Flipping an object, part or SVG across an axis (“Mirror along the X Axis”, “Mirror horizontally”). It transforms the object in place — unlike Clone, nothing new is created. The bare “Mirror” is a short input label in the SVG/emboss tool.	Mirall
Primitive	A built-in basic shape (cube, cylinder, sphere, ...) that can be added to the plate.	Primitiva
Access Code	The code shown on the printer that authorizes a LAN connection to it.	Clau d'Accés
Plugin	An add-on software component that extends the application (e.g. the network plug-in).	Connector
Dialog	A UI dialog box. Translate the "dialog box" sense, not the "dialogue"/conversation sense.	Quadre de diàleg
Outline	The outer boundary line of a shape or selection.	Contorn
Wireframe	A see-through view showing only a model's edges, not solid surfaces.	Malla alàmbrica
Top (Camera View)	Navigator-cube face / View-menu item that looks straight down at the plate. Camera sense — not the Top of the printed part.	Superior
Bottom (Camera View)	Navigator-cube face / View-menu item that looks up from below. Camera sense — not the Bottom of the printed part.	Inferior
Front (Camera View)	Navigator-cube face / View-menu item that looks at the front of the plate.	Frontal
Back (Camera View)	Navigator-cube face that looks from behind (msgctxt “Camera View”). The direction “behind” — NOT the “go back / return” button, which is “Back” with msgctxt “Navigation”. The View menu calls the same direction “Rear”.	Darrera
Left (Camera View)	Navigator-cube face / View-menu item that looks from the left (msgctxt “Camera View”). Not the left nozzle or text alignment.	Esquerra
Right (Camera View)	Navigator-cube face / View-menu item that looks from the right (msgctxt “Camera View”). Not the right nozzle or text alignment.	Dreta
Internal solid infill	The 100%-dense infill under top surfaces and above bottom ones, as opposed to Sparse infill.	Farciment sòlid intern
Wipe	Wiping the nozzle tip clean / relieving nozzle pressure. Distinct from Flush / Purge, which clears the previous material out of the nozzle channel.	Netejar
Support interface	The denser layers between the support and the model surface it touches. Not the prime-tower Interface layer.	Interfície de suport
Model	A whole 3D object on the plate. Where a string covers both a model and its parts, prefer the neutral "object".	Model
Part	A component of a model. Where a string covers both a model and its parts, prefer the neutral "object".	Peça
Volume	A solid body making up a model; a negative volume is a cut-out. Not the numeric volume measurement.	Volum
Texture	The image painted onto a surface (custom plate image, model UV map) - not the *textured* rough finish of a plate, fuzzy skin or top surface, which is a different word in most languages.	Textura
Gizmo	An on-canvas manipulation tool (move/scale/rotate handles, cut, paint...).	Gizmo
Adaptive bed mesh	Bed levelling that probes only the area the print occupies, instead of the whole bed.	Malla de placa adaptativa
Damping	The damping ratio used by input shaping when computing damped oscillations.	Esmorteïment
Snake	Object-instance print order that walks the plate in a serpentine, row-by-row path (refined with 2-opt). The movement pattern — not the animal, and distinct from the Zig Zag infill pattern.	Serpentí
Nearest-neighbor	The default object-instance ordering heuristic: each next instance is the closest one not yet visited (“nearest-neighbor chaining”, then refined with 2-opt). It has no standalone msgid — it appears inside the print-order tooltip. Not the “Nearest” seam position, which is a different setting.	Veí més proper
Design (tab)	The main tab for parametric CAD modelling, next to Prepare and Preview; "New Design" starts a new model there.	Disseny
Sketch	A 2D drawing (lines, arcs, circles, splines) made on a plane or a face in the Design tab, which features such as Extrude or Revolve turn into a solid.	Esbós
Constraint	A geometric or dimensional rule between sketch entities (horizontal, parallel, tangent, coincident, a fixed distance…) that the sketch solver keeps satisfied.	Restricció
Dimension (sketch)	A driving measurement (length, distance, radius, angle) placed on sketch geometry; editing its value resizes the sketch. Not the object's size ("Dimensions").	Cota
Construction geometry	Sketch lines and arcs used only as references for drawing and constraints; they are not part of the profile. Toggled with "Construction".	Geometria de construcció
Extrude	Design-tab feature that pushes a closed sketch profile, or a picked face, along a straight direction to add or remove material. Not the G-code viewer's Extrude move type.	Extrusió
Revolve	Design-tab feature that spins a sketch profile around an axis to make a solid of revolution.	Revolució
